title: The right proper Kan-Quillen model structure
statement: On the category of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] let $\Delta^n$ be the representable $\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$, let $\partial\Delta^n$ be the union of its proper faces, and for $n\geq1$ let $\Lambda_i^n$ be the union of all faces except the $i$th, $0\leq i\leq n$. A weak homotopy equivalence is a map whose geometric realization induces a bijection on path components and isomorphisms of all homotopy groups at all basepoints. There is a functorial model structure with these weak equivalences, degreewise injective maps as cofibrations, and maps with the right lifting property against every $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ as fibrations (Kan fibrations). Its fibrant objects are the Kan complexes. A map is a trivial fibration exactly when it has the right lifting property against every $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Every monomorphism is a transfinite composite of pushouts of coproducts of boundary inclusions. Trivial cofibrations are the retracts of transfinite composites of pushouts of coproducts of horn inclusions. Pullback of any weak homotopy equivalence along any Kan fibration is a weak homotopy equivalence (right properness). A homotopy pullback of a cospan of Kan complexes is represented by replacing one leg by a weak equivalence followed by a fibration, and then taking the ordinary pullback. The resulting space is independent, up to natural equivalence, of this replacement.

proof.text: Consider the ordinary category of Kan complexes with the restrictions of $W$ and $F$. Its terminal object is Kan. Maps to the terminal object belong to $F$; composition and base change preserve $F$ because a horn lifting problem reduces to the corresponding lifting problem before composition or pullback. A pullback of Kan complexes along a fibration is Kan by composing its fibration to its Kan base with the map to the terminal object. Trivial fibrations are $I^{\pitchfork}$ by the core theorem, so they too are stable under pullback by the same lifting argument. The functorial $(C\cap W,F)$ factorization of a map between Kan complexes has Kan intermediate object, since its second leg is a fibration over a Kan complex. All the hypotheses of the fibrant-category localization theorem are now verified. It follows that localization sends each strict pullback along a fibration between Kan complexes to a limiting coherent square, naturally as a cone.

For $A\to C\leftarrow B$ with $A,B,C$ Kan, factor the first leg as $A\xrightarrow{w}A'\xrightarrow{p}C$ with $w\in W$ and $p\in F$. The object $A'$ and the strict pullback $P=A'\times_CB$ are Kan, as in the preceding step. The image of this strict pullback cone is limiting by the preceding step. Let $D$ and $D'$ be the two cospan diagrams and let $\alpha:D\to D'$ have components $w,1_C,1_B$. Every component is an equivalence, so the enhanced functor-and-cone calculus makes $\alpha$ an equivalence in the cospan functor quasicategory; choose an inverse $\beta$ and the coherent inverse homotopies supplied there. Postcomposition with $\alpha$ sends a cone $\Delta_Kx\to D$ to a cone $\Delta_Kx\to D'$, while postcomposition with $\beta$ sends cones back, and the two coherent inverse homotopies give mutually inverse equivalences of the two cone quasicategories. Equivalences of mapping spaces therefore carry terminal cones to terminal cones, so the limiting cone on $P$ for $D'$ transports to a limiting cone for $D$. The same argument works for any weak-equivalence/fibration factorization of either leg. The full subcategory of terminal cones is a contractible Kan complex by the cone calculus; hence the space of comparisons of any two transported limiting cones is contractible. These comparisons are natural in maps of cospans, with the higher compatibilities supplied by the same coherent inverse homotopies. This is independence as a space with its limiting cone, not a claim of a preferred strict isomorphism of simplicial sets.
